input_signals.name: CashBurnFundedExternalFinance
input_signals.expression: MUL(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross external capital raising (equity plus long-term debt issuance) is benign for cash-generating firms but signals funding stress and dilution risk when the firm has been burning operating cash for several years.
input_signals.reasoning: The continuous rank weight acts as a soft gate that up-weights issuance precisely for the weakest cash-flow firms while shrinking it toward zero for self-funding firms, so the signal isolates stress-driven financing rather than growth-driven financing. Averaging operating cash flow over three years measures a persistent funding deficit rather than a transitory working-capital swing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ImprovingQualityRepurchaser
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(prstkc, at)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Buybacks are most informative about mispricing when the firm's operating cash-flow profitability is on an improving multi-year trajectory that the market has not yet extrapolated; buybacks from firms with deteriorating fundamentals are defensive EPS management.
input_signals.reasoning: The trend operator captures the direction of fundamental quality rather than its level, so the interaction separates "improving firm buying its own stock" from "declining firm propping up EPS," which pure repurchase-yield signals conflate. The low end of the signal, weak buyback activity plus deteriorating cash-flow trend, is the natural short leg.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( prstkc, at ) ), rank( trend( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: PayoutCredibilityGate
input_signals.expression: MUL(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at), IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The same act of distributing cash carries opposite information depending on the firm's cash-generating quality: distributions by firms with above-peer operating cash-flow profitability signal genuine excess capital and undervaluation, whereas equally large distributions by firms with below-peer cash profitability are unsustainable capital depletion that must be reversed through later cuts or external raising.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing leg is a one-sided distribution intensity and the quality leg is an industry-centered z-score, so the marginal effect of paying out literally changes sign across quality states rather than stacking two same-signed anomaly ranks; non-distributing firms sit near zero and neither tail is populated by "uninformative" cases. The short tail is specifically weak-cash-flow heavy distributors, an economically distinct group from generic low-profitability firms, and industry centering removes the mechanical loading on the profitability factor that made the prior version a near-linear composite.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ratio( add( prstkc, dvc ), at ), ind_zscore( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: IssuanceAgainstDepletedRetainedEarnings
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), RANK(NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: External financing is benign for firms that have accumulated a stock of retained profits (they raise capital from a position of strength) and toxic for firms whose balance sheets show little or negative accumulated earnings, since those firms are financing losses rather than opportunities.
input_signals.reasoning: This swaps the flow-based cash-burn gate for a stock-based lifecycle quality gate, testing whether the accumulated-profit state conditions issuance more sharply than the current cash-flow rate, which the FF5 profitability factor may partly absorb. Retained earnings over assets is slow-moving, so the resulting portfolio composition should be more stable than a gate driven by volatile annual cash flow.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ), 1 ), rank( neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: VolatilityGatedNetExternalFinance
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), 1), RANK(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The information in net external financing depends on the reliability of the firm's cash-generating process: for firms with stable operating cash flow, raising or returning capital is routine treasury activity, whereas for firms with volatile cash flow, net capital raising signals that a fragile business is leaning on markets and net capital return signals genuine surplus.
input_signals.reasoning: The gate is a second-moment quality measure rather than a level, so it is orthogonal to the profitability and investment factors in FF5 and tests an untried conditioning channel: fundamental instability as the amplifier of financing news. Because the financing leg is signed and the gate is non-negative, the slope steepens with instability rather than flipping sign for stable firms, which keeps every quadrant economically interpretable.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), 1 ), rank( vol( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: CredibleDeleveraging
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at), 1), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt retirement is valuable news when the retiring firm is both highly levered (so the credit risk reduction is material) and cash-generative (so the retirement is funded from operations rather than from asset sales or dilution); the same repayment by an unlevered or cash-poor firm carries little information.
input_signals.reasoning: LeverageStrainedDebtIssuance failed largely because its signed gate collapsed to zero for the mid-strain majority, leaving a thin, noisy sort; here the weight is a non-negative two-channel rank sum that is only large where deleveraging is both material and self-funded, giving a better-identified long leg. It also tests the deleveraging side of the credit channel, which the archive has probed only implicitly through issuance signals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( dltr, dltis ), at ), 1 ), sumrank( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: DilutionWithoutProductivity
input_signals.expression: MUL(GROWTH(csho, 1), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(sale, at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Share issuance is defensible when the asset base is being put to more productive use and destructive when each new dollar of equity funds assets that generate less revenue than before; deteriorating asset turnover is the quality state that converts dilution into value transfer away from existing holders.
input_signals.reasoning: The conditioning variable is a change in operating efficiency rather than a profitability or cash-flow level, so unlike the archive's gates it is not a close cousin of the RMW factor that absorbed prior alphas. Using share count growth rather than the sstk cash-flow line also captures dilution from acquisitions and option exercise, which broadens coverage relative to the gen-0 and gen-1 issuance legs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( growth( csho, 1 ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( sale, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: BuybackFundingSource
input_signals.expression: MUL(RATIO(prstkc, at), SUB(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(dltis, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The credibility of a repurchase depends on where the cash comes from: buybacks funded out of recurring operating cash flow signal genuine surplus and management confidence, while buybacks executed alongside heavy long-term borrowing are balance-sheet engineering that raises fragility without conveying valuation information.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a genuine three-way interaction in which a second financing variable, not a quality variable, flips the sign of the first, so the long leg is internally funded shrinkers and the short leg is debt-financed shrinkers — a contrast orthogonal to RMW and therefore a candidate fix for the weak alphas of ImprovingQualityRepurchaser and PayoutCredibilityGate. The signed gate is zero for firms whose funding profile is ambiguous, concentrating the sort on cleanly classifiable cases.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ratio( prstkc, at ), sub( rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), rank( ratio( dltis, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: BuybackAtOwnCashFlowPeak
input_signals.expression: MUL(RATIO(prstkc, at), SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at), 5), RANK(RATIO(dltis, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A repurchase is credible when the firm is buying stock at a moment when its own cash generation is unusually strong by its own standards and it is not borrowing to do so; the same repurchase executed when internal cash flow is at a personal low and long-term debt is being drawn is balance-sheet engineering.
input_signals.reasoning: Rather than broadening the archive's best signal, this isolates the single design question its result leaves open — whether the alpha comes from the cross-sectional profitability rank (which is RMW-like and could be a factor artifact) or from the genuine funding-source contrast — by replacing the cross-sectional cash-flow rank with the firm's own five-year cash-flow position. If the alpha survives with a within-firm internal-funding measure, the mechanism is timing and funding credibility rather than a profitability tilt, which is the more valuable finding for the remaining generations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ratio( prstkc, at ), sub( ts_rank( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ), rank( ratio( dltis, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ExpansionFundingSource
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(GROWTH(at, 1), INDICATOR(GROWTH(at, 1), 0)), SUB(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Growth is not intrinsically good or bad; what matters is who paid for it. Expansion financed out of operating cash flow reflects a business reinvesting its own surplus, while identical expansion financed by outside capital reflects management appetite unconstrained by internal performance and is systematically overpriced at the time of the raise.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves the funding-source principle that produced the archive's only joint FMB-and-alpha result from the payout side to the investment side, a genuinely different economic decision, and it is not the accruals-times-issuance construction the critic identified as a re-test of DilutionQualityGate. The indicator restricts the action leg to firms that actually expanded, so both tails are growing firms distinguished only by funding source, while shrinking firms sit at zero in the middle rather than forming a tied mass in either leg.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( growth( at, 1 ), indicator( growth( at, 1 ), 0 ) ), sub( rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), rank( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: RawSurplusGatedExpansion
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(GROWTH(at, 1), INDICATOR(GROWTH(at, 1), 0)), WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: What makes expansion credible is the actual cash surplus behind it — operating cash flow minus outside capital absorbed, measured in dollars per unit of assets — rather than the firm's relative standing on two separate cross-sectional rankings.
input_signals.reasoning: This isolates one design choice in the archive's best signal: the rank-difference gate is replaced by the economically literal funding surplus, which preserves magnitude information (a firm covering expansion twice over versus barely) that ranking discards, and simultaneously strips out the cross-sectional profitability rank that makes the current gate partly an RMW proxy. Comparing its alpha against ExpansionFundingSource tells us whether the winner's power comes from measured funding capacity or from relative-profitability sorting, which determines how the remaining generations should refine the gate.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( growth( at, 1 ), indicator( growth( at, 1 ), 0 ) ), winsor( sub( ratio( oancf, at ), ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: ErraticFinancingWeakMargins
input_signals.expression: MUL(VOL(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), 5), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm whose net capital flow swings violently from raising to returning and back has no stable financing policy, which in a low-gross-margin business signals that funding decisions are reactive to operating shortfalls rather than planned; such reactive financing predicts poor returns even when the average net flow is near zero.
input_signals.reasoning: This targets a quantity that every directional financing signal in the archive averages away — the instability of the policy rather than its direction — and gates it on gross margin, a quality dimension the archive has never used and which is not a cash-flow or distress proxy. It is the one exploratory slot in the batch, testing whether financing *variability* interacted with operating economics carries information distinct from financing level.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( vol( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), 5 ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: DualChannelDeploymentFundingSource
input_signals.expression: MUL(SUMRANK(MUL(GROWTH(at, 1), INDICATOR(GROWTH(at, 1), 0)), RATIO(prstkc, at)), SUB(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms deploy capital either into the asset base or into retiring their own shares, and breadth across both channels is itself informative: a firm expanding and repurchasing simultaneously is making a wide commitment, and the credibility of that commitment depends entirely on whether operations or outside investors funded it.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the raw sum with SUMRANK puts asset growth and repurchase intensity on a common unit-interval footing, so the composite scale genuinely reflects deployment across both channels instead of being numerically swamped by asset growth as the critic noted. This makes it a real breadth test against ExpansionFundingSource: if the ranked dual-channel scale improves alpha and t-stat, deployment breadth adds information beyond the single strongest channel.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( sumrank( mul( growth( at, 1 ), indicator( growth( at, 1 ), 0 ) ), ratio( prstkc, at ) ), sub( rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), rank( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: FinancingRegimeGatedExpansion
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(GROWTH(at, 1), INDICATOR(GROWTH(at, 1), 0)), SUB(RANK(TS_SUM(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), RANK(TS_SUM(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: What the market misprices may be the firm's financing *regime* rather than this year's financing event: a firm that has covered its needs from operations for three straight years and now expands is a proven compounder, whereas a firm that has repeatedly returned to the capital markets is expanding on borrowed conviction even if this particular year's raise looks modest.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a neutralization knob but a test of the economic horizon over which funding credibility operates — contemporaneous mix versus multi-year regime — and the archive gives a genuine reason to ask: the standalone five-year self-funding gap was weak (alpha 1.4%) while the one-year gate inside the expansion signal was strong, leaving open whether accumulating the gate helps or dilutes. A regime gate also changes portfolio membership slowly, which should improve the stability that one-year financing sorts have lacked.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( growth( at, 1 ), indicator( growth( at, 1 ), 0 ) ), sub( rank( ts_sum( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), rank( ts_sum( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: LongLivedInvestmentFundingSurplus
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(at, 1), DELTA(act, 1)), at), INDICATOR(SUB(DELTA(at, 1), DELTA(act, 1)), 0)), WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: The funding-source question bites hardest for irreversible commitments: growth in long-lived, non-current assets cannot be unwound if the cash flow fails to appear, so externally financed fixed-asset expansion is far more likely to be value-destroying than an externally financed build in receivables and inventory, which self-liquidates within a year.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive winner uses total asset growth, which mixes reversible working-capital swings with irreversible capital commitments; isolating the non-current component identifies the deployment for which management's funding discipline actually matters. If alpha improves, the mechanism is sharpened from "growth" to "irreversible investment," which is a substantive economic refinement rather than a rescaling.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( ratio( sub( delta( at, 1 ), delta( act, 1 ) ), at ), indicator( sub( delta( at, 1 ), delta( act, 1 ) ), 0 ) ), winsor( sub( ratio( oancf, at ), ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: NetMarketDependenceGatedExpansion
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(GROWTH(at, 1), INDICATOR(GROWTH(at, 1), 0)), WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: What matters for funding credibility is the outside capital a firm actually absorbs on net, not the gross flows it runs through the treasury: a firm that borrows and simultaneously repays, or issues shares while retiring others, has not become market-dependent, whereas gross-flow measures label it as such.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the dividend perturbation the critic correctly called immaterial with a first-order change to the gate's financing leg — gross raising becomes net absorption — which reclassifies exactly the refinancing and churn population the archive has shown behaves differently (DebtRolloverChurn, TwoWayEquityChurn). If the alpha improves, market dependence is about net capital absorbed; if it deteriorates, the gross-flow version is capturing the frictional cost of touching markets at all, which is an equally informative answer.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( growth( at, 1 ), indicator( growth( at, 1 ), 0 ) ), winsor( sub( ratio( oancf, at ), ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: SelfFundedExpanderRegime
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(GROWTH(at, 1), INDICATOR(GROWTH(at, 1), 0)), SUB(INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)), 0), INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), RATIO(oancf, at)), 0)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Self-funding is a discrete state rather than a continuous quantity: an expanding firm either covers its growth from operations or it does not, and the market's mistake is failing to classify the firm into the right regime, not mismeasuring by how much the surplus exceeded zero.
input_signals.reasoning: Rather than crossbreeding two archive members, this asks whether the winner's information lives in the sign or the magnitude of the funding surplus, by replacing the continuous gate with a clean plus-one/minus-one regime classifier while holding the deployment scale fixed. It also directly addresses the outlier sensitivity of the raw-times-raw product the critic flagged in the accepted winner: if a bounded classifier reproduces the alpha, the mechanism is robust regime membership rather than a few extreme surplus observations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( growth( at, 1 ), indicator( growth( at, 1 ), 0 ) ), sub( indicator( sub( ratio( oancf, at ), ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ) ), 0 ), indicator( sub( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ), ratio( oancf, at ) ), 0 ) ) )

input_signals.name: ExternalCapitalPerUnitOfGrossProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(GROWTH(at, 1), INDICATOR(GROWTH(at, 1), 0)), WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), SUB(sale, cogs)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: The right yardstick for market dependence is the firm's own earning engine: raising an amount equal to several years of gross profit to fund expansion is a fundamentally different act from raising a token amount, and expansions requiring large multiples of the margin engine are the ones that disappoint.
input_signals.reasoning: Expressing the gate as a ratio of financing to gross profit rather than a difference removes the scale-mismatch degeneracy the critic identified — the quantity cannot collapse into gross profitability because the numerator is purely a financing flow — while keeping gross profit's stability advantage over noisy annual cash flow. Gross profit is positive for the overwhelming majority of firms, so the ratio is well behaved without the sign-flip pathology that afflicted earlier cash-flow-denominated coverage ratios.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( growth( at, 1 ), indicator( growth( at, 1 ), 0 ) ), winsor( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), sub( sale, cogs ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: PureExpanderFundingRegime
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(GROWTH(at, 1), 0), SUB(INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)), 0), INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), RATIO(oancf, at)), 0)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The entire mispricing may be a three-state classification — self-funded expander, market-funded expander, everyone else — with the amount of expansion adding nothing once the funding regime is known.
input_signals.reasoning: Every strong archive signal still multiplies by continuous asset growth, which means its long leg is tilted toward the most aggressive growers and its spread partly inherits the investment anomaly; removing the magnitude entirely tests whether the funding classification alone carries the alpha. If it does, the resulting signal is fully bounded, essentially immune to outliers and rebalancing lumpiness, and cleanly separable from CMA — the most defensible version of the mechanism to carry into the final generations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( growth( at, 1 ), 0 ), sub( indicator( sub( ratio( oancf, at ), ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ) ), 0 ), indicator( sub( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ), ratio( oancf, at ) ), 0 ) ) )

input_signals.name: EquityChannelFundingSurplus
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(GROWTH(at, 1), INDICATOR(GROWTH(at, 1), 0)), WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity is the informationally sensitive instrument: managers with private good news borrow, and those exploiting rich valuations sell shares, so expansion funded by net equity issuance should be far more damaging than expansion funded by borrowing.
input_signals.reasoning: The gate has so far pooled equity and debt, leaving unresolved which instrument carries the signal; restricting it to net equity flow isolates the adverse-selection channel and, if it matches or beats the pooled gate, tells us the debt component is dilutive noise. This is a decomposition of a validated mechanism rather than a rescaling, and it also drops the debt-refinancing churn that the archive has repeatedly shown to be mechanical.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( growth( at, 1 ), indicator( growth( at, 1 ), 0 ) ), winsor( sub( ratio( oancf, at ), ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: PayoutFundingRegime
input_signals.expression: MUL(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at), SUB(INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), dltr), at)), 0), INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), dltr), at), RATIO(oancf, at)), 0)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Distributions carry information only when the distributing firm is genuinely in surplus after its net dealings with capital markets; a firm handing cash to shareholders while absorbing capital elsewhere in the capital structure is recycling investor money and its payout should be discounted entirely.
input_signals.reasoning: The payout channel has produced modest alphas throughout (1-3.5%) using continuous or rank-based quality gates, and the regime classifier that lifted the expansion signal to a 4.19 t-stat has never been applied to it, so this is a genuine test rather than a restatement. The gate excludes repurchases and dividends from the financing side, so no variable appears on both sides of the interaction and the classification cannot be mechanically induced by the payout itself.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ratio( add( prstkc, dvc ), at ), sub( indicator( sub( ratio( oancf, at ), ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), dltr ), at ) ), 0 ), indicator( sub( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), dltr ), at ), ratio( oancf, at ) ), 0 ) ) )

input_signals.name: ExternalFundingShareOfExpansion
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(GROWTH(at, 1), 0), WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), oancf), DELTA(at, 1)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: The economically meaningful quantity is what fraction of this year's balance-sheet growth had to be paid for by outside investors after internal cash was exhausted; growth that required markets to fund most of the increment is systematically overpriced, while growth whose increment was more than covered by operations is underpriced.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a crossing of the two tested gates but a change of functional form: because the sort is restricted to expanders, the asset increment is a strictly positive denominator, so the ratio measures the *share* of the deployment financed externally rather than a difference of asset-scaled flows — a scale-free quantity that treats a large firm adding 5% of assets and a small one adding 40% identically. It also avoids the critic's collapse problem, since firms are spread continuously across the ratio instead of being pooled into a dominant plus-one state, with non-expanders sitting at zero between the two economically meaningful tails.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( growth( at, 1 ), 0 ), winsor( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), oancf ), delta( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: AccountingFundsSelfFundedExpansion
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(GROWTH(at, 1), INDICATOR(GROWTH(at, 1), 0)), WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), dvc), at), RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, dvc))), at)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Self-funding can be reconstructed entirely from the income statement and balance sheet: retained funds from operations after dividends, measured against the year's increase in debt plus the increase in book equity that earnings did not produce, which is the capital the firm absorbed from outside investors.
input_signals.reasoning: Both sides of the gate are now scaled by assets, so the expression computes the stated internal-versus-external funding difference in consistent units, repairing the dimensional inconsistency caused by mixing a share-count percentage with asset-scaled flows. The motivation is unchanged and remains the strongest in the batch: every archive gate depends on cash-flow-statement items that cap coverage near 0.08, whereas earnings, depreciation, dividends, debt and book equity are available for a far wider panel, so surviving alpha here buys both robustness and a much larger tradable universe.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( growth( at, 1 ), indicator( growth( at, 1 ), 0 ) ), winsor( sub( ratio( sub( add( ib, dp ), dvc ), at ), ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), sub( ib, dvc ) ) ), at ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: AccountingFundsRegimeExpansion
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(GROWTH(at, 1), INDICATOR(GROWTH(at, 1), 0)), SUB(INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), dvc), at), RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, dvc))), at)), 0), INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, dvc))), at), RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), dvc), at)), 0)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Whether retained funds from operations covered the year's absorption of outside capital is a discrete state, and classifying that state from income-statement and balance-sheet data alone should carry the same information as the cash-flow-statement version while applying to a far larger population of firms.
input_signals.reasoning: The accounting-funds construction gave the archive's strongest FMB slope (4.85) at coverage 0.126 but only a 2.4% alpha, while in the cash-flow family the switch from a continuous surplus to a sign-only classifier raised the alpha t-stat from 3.74 to 4.19 by removing dependence on a noisy tail of surplus magnitudes.
